The hub's agreement cut-offs

Source: R/metrics.R
agreement_thresholds.Rd

The cut-offs the hub's cross-engine comparison applied when it called a parameter concordant, with the hub's own defaults. That comparison, triangulate(), was removed from flexyBayes in version 0.14.0; the source lines cited below are from flexyBayes 0.10.0. A parameter is concordant when the absolute mean difference is at most mean_shift_sd_max reference SDs, the Wasserstein-1 distance is at most w1_sd_max reference SDs, and the ratio of the two posterior SDs lies inside sd_ratio_band; any breach makes it discordant.

Usage

agreement_thresholds(
  mean_shift_sd_max = 0.1,
  w1_sd_max = 0.1,
  sd_ratio_band = c(0.9, 1.1),
  quantile_probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)

Arguments

mean_shift_sd_max

Single positive number: the largest absolute difference in posterior means, in reference-SD units, a concordant parameter may show. Hub default 0.1, from .FB_TRIANGULATE_MEAN_SHIFT_MAX at flexyBayes 0.10.0 R/triangulate.R:757.

w1_sd_max

Single positive number: the largest Wasserstein-1 distance, in reference-SD units, a concordant parameter may show. Hub default 0.1, from .FB_TRIANGULATE_W1_MAX at R/triangulate.R:758.

sd_ratio_band

Numeric vector of length two, increasing: the band the ratio of the two posterior SDs must lie in. Hub default c(0.9, 1.1), from .FB_TRIANGULATE_SD_RATIO_BAND at R/triangulate.R:759.

quantile_probs

Numeric vector of length two, increasing, inside (0, 1): the quantiles whose difference is reported. Hub default c(0.025, 0.975), from the stats::quantile() calls in .triangulate_one at R/triangulate.R:495 and R/triangulate.R:497.

Value

A named list with the four elements above.

Details

The cut-offs are heuristics in the sense the Bayesian-workflow literature uses for cross-implementation checks: they are set to flag a difference a reader should look at, they are not derived from a sampling distribution, and they carry no error rate. The hub documents them that way and quorum inherits both the numbers and the reading.

quantile_probs names the two quantiles whose difference the table reports as q025_diff and q975_diff. The hub reports that tail drift without ever thresholding it, so there is no quantile tolerance in the verdict rule; the argument fixes which quantiles are reported, not a cut-off they must clear.

See also

agreement_pairwise(), agreement_status().

Examples

agreement_thresholds()
#> $mean_shift_sd_max
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $w1_sd_max
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $sd_ratio_band
#> [1] 0.9 1.1
#> 
#> $quantile_probs
#> [1] 0.025 0.975
#> 
agreement_thresholds(w1_sd_max = 0.05)
#> $mean_shift_sd_max
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $w1_sd_max
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $sd_ratio_band
#> [1] 0.9 1.1
#> 
#> $quantile_probs
#> [1] 0.025 0.975
#>
